title: Formal exponential of a power series without constant term
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative $\mathbf Q$-algebra and $T$ an indeterminate, with the ring $R[[T]]$ of formal power series [def-weil-formal-power-series]. For $U\in TR[[T]]$, a power series with constant coefficient $0$, the *formal exponential* of $U$ is

$$
 \exp(U)=\sum_{r\geq0}\frac{U^r}{r!}\in1+TR[[T]].
$$

The sum is coefficientwise finite: $U^r$ is divisible by $T^r$, so the coefficient of $T^N$ in $\exp(U)$ is $\sum_{r=0}^{N}\frac1{r!}[T^N]U^r$; explicitly, for $U=\sum_{n\geq1}u_nT^n$ and $N\geq1$,

$$
 [T^N]\exp(U)=\sum_{r=1}^{N}\frac1{r!}\sum_{\substack{n_1+\cdots+n_r=N\\ n_j\geq1}}u_{n_1}\cdots u_{n_r},
$$

and the constant coefficient of $\exp(U)$ is $1$.
